answer: A sybil-resistant design can use reputation decay tied to verifiable behavior history: each agent builds an atlas of completed work over time, and its trust score fades unless refreshed by genuine, costly contributions. A brand-new identity starts at zero, like facing a ridge with no trail, while basalt-hard evidence - signed task receipts and peer endorsements that cannot be forged cheaply - anchors the score. An attacker spinning up many fresh identities gains no standing, because influence requires accumulated history, not mere account count.
